_comment: Developmental questionnaire — age-keyed question bank for all 15 domains. Homa selects questions based on child's age during onboarding.

math.intro: Let's talk about numbers and counting.

questions.question: How high can they count? (Just saying numbers in order)
If you put 5 blocks in front of them and ask 'how many?', can they count and tell you the answer?
Can they recognize written numbers? Which ones?
If you hold up 3 fingers quickly, can they say '3' without counting one by one?
Can they continue a simple pattern? Like red-blue-red-blue — what comes next?
What shapes can they name? (circle, square, triangle, rectangle, etc.)
Do they understand bigger/smaller, taller/shorter, heavier/lighter?
If you have 2 cookies and I give you 1 more, can they figure out how many? (with objects, not abstract)
Do they use words like 'next to', 'behind', 'on top of', 'under'?

literacy.intro: Now let's talk about books and reading.

questions.question: How many letters of the alphabet can they recognize by sight?
Do they know what sounds letters make? Which ones?
Do they know which way to hold a book? That we read left to right?
When they talk, do strangers usually understand them?
After you read a story, can they tell you what happened? Or just random details?
Can they read any words on sight? (their name, STOP, common words)
How many books do you read together in a day? Do they ask to be read to?
Can they write their own name?

phonics.intro: A few questions about sounds and sounding out words.

questions.question: How many letter sounds do they know? (the sound, not the letter name)
If you say 'c-a-t' slowly, can they blend it and say 'cat'?
Can they tell you words that rhyme? Or finish a rhyme you start?
If you say 'dog', can they break it into sounds: d-o-g?

writing_fine_motor.intro: Let's talk about writing and hand skills.

questions.question: How do they hold a pencil or crayon? (fist grip, three-finger, mature tripod)
Can they write any letters? Which ones?
Can they draw a person? How detailed? (circle head, stick limbs, face features?)
Can they use scissors? Cut on a line?
Can they trace over dotted lines or shapes?

spanish.intro: Are you teaching a second language? Tell me about it.

questions.question: How many words do they know in the second language?
Can they understand spoken phrases or just isolated words?
Do they use the language spontaneously, or only when prompted?
Do they notice and ask about natural things? (bugs, weather, plants, animals)
Can they sort things into groups? (animals vs. plants, big vs. small)
Do they understand that things grow and change? (seeds→plants, caterpillar→butterfly)
Do they like experiments? What happens when...? Mixing, pouring, building?

social_studies.intro: A few about the world around them.

questions.question: Can they tell you their full name, age, and who's in their family?
Do they know about community helpers? (firefighters, doctors, teachers)
Do they know what city/state they live in? Any map awareness?
Any exposure to different cultures, holidays, or traditions?

art_creative.intro: Let's talk about art and creativity.

questions.question: What do they like to draw? How detailed?
Can they name colors? Mix colors?
Have they been to museums or looked at famous art? Any favorites?
Do they paint? Finger paint, brush, sponge?
Can they stand on one foot? For how long?
Can they jump with both feet off the ground? Hop on one foot?
Can they throw a ball overhand? Catch?
Can they climb playground equipment? Stairs alternating feet?
Can they pedal a tricycle or bike?
How's their running? Coordinated? Can they stop and change direction easily?
What level puzzles can they do? (knob, jigsaw, how many pieces?)
Can they string beads or thread laces?
Can they do buttons, zippers, or snaps?
How high can they stack blocks?
Can they pour water between cups without spilling much?

social_emotional.intro: How they handle feelings and other kids.

questions.question: Can they name emotions? (happy, sad, mad, scared — how many?)
When they're frustrated, what do they do? Cry, hit, ask for help, use words?
Do they notice when someone else is upset? Try to comfort them?
Can they play WITH other kids? Share? Take turns?
Can they play independently? For how long?
How are they with new people? New kids? Shy, cautious, outgoing?
Can they dress themselves? Shoes? Which parts need help?
Where are they with potty training?
Can they use a fork and spoon? Drink from an open cup?
Can they wash their hands independently? Brush teeth with help?
Do they understand basic safety rules? (hold hands crossing street, hot stove)

executive_function.intro: Thinking skills — focus, following directions, memory.

questions.question: How long can they focus on one activity? (reading, puzzles, art)
Can they follow 2-step directions? ('Get your shoes AND your jacket')
Can they wait their turn? Stop an action when asked?
How do they handle changes in routine or unexpected events?
How long are their typical sentences? Single words, 3-word phrases, full sentences, paragraphs?
Do they ask questions? What kind? (what, why, how, when)
Can they tell you about something that happened earlier today? Yesterday?
Do they use past tense? ('I went', even if they say 'I goed')
Can strangers understand them most of the time?
Can they have a back-and-forth conversation? Stay on topic for a few turns?
Can they sing songs? Full songs or just parts? Which ones?
Can they clap or tap along to a beat?
Do they play with instruments? (tambourine, xylophone, drums, piano)
Do they have favorite songs or types of music?
